verdict.tagline: A thrilling descent into horror with memorable action and tense encounters.
for_you_if: you love classic survival horror puzzle boxes
not_for_you_if: you need modern inventory auto-sort features
you require smooth third-person character movement
you want perfectly balanced high-difficulty runs

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features an in-game shop and weapon upgrade mechanics.

citations.review_text: gameplay wise you can tell the development team experimented in unique mechanics, especially the 'shop' mechanic that actually hold quite while, balanced and engaging. its still typical collect resources , shoot and follow the path given to you. still like the re7 recipe , environment and graphics is 10/10 but the shooting ragdolls and gore is worst then re7 , its like 'toned down' as to the main bosses and their 'areas' some were lacking a little, but there some major 'bosses' that is excellently presented in all cases, spoiler wise the story still feels shallow like re7 until the end you will tear a little but, its already obvious what the resolution and conflict is..  re7 was more fresh as it is the first game and not a sequel, overall a great resident evil cinema must rec

really fun game. on a much lighter tone than RE7. so many game mechanics are better. includes merchant, weapon upgrades, handgun ammo and heals dont share ingredients now, can use F to break crates and much more, none of which was in RE7.

looks really good too compared to RE7 and lets not forget the dommy mommy

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the default field of view (FOV) setting feels restricted or causes discomfort, requiring settings adjustments or a third-party mod to play comfortably.

citations.review_text:
Overall RE village is really fun to play, although i have my gripes with some things.

For example, Chris just not telling us anything about what is going on, and seeming like the bad guy until he reveals it, and even then its quite late in the story.
The last bossfight and ending just didnt do it for me, felt weak and bossfight was underwhelming.
FOV. Being locked to such a nauseous FOV was horrible, had to get an FOV mod after 1 hour of playing, otherwise i would have refunded it.

Everything else though, the graphics, the characters, the different areas, all very beautiful and fun  to explore. Except the dolls, ♥♥♥♥ the dolls.

Solid 7.5/10, would get it on sale if you can, if you try to explore everything the game is still only like 12 hours.

My favorite game in the series so far, but I'd still give it a 6/10 because of the lack of settings. The absence of an FOV slider made me feel nauseous playing at my normal PC setup, so I switched to playing on my TV with a controller, which made for a much more comfortable experience.

Really enjoyed this game. I've been powering through the whole Series. so far after completing this game it's probably my 2nd favorite. I haven't played the new one yet. The pacing was great the puzzles were good. I had to mess around with some settings to make the 1st view feel right. But really enjoyed the story. Great game. worth playing.

citations.review_text:
I hope we have the chance to play as Mia, a mother story, I know she is cured now, but at least stealth game like Ashley on RE4.
This game let the player play as Rose (Daughter), and Chris, I wish we have the chance to play Rebecca Chambers too or at least a cameo.
I am looking forward to fight Lycans with mount seen in first visit of village but i never saw them after. 
The game tells you that you can ONLY be the best Dad if you sacrifice yourself for your child otherwise you wouldn't get the Dad related achievements

PROS
-No woke
-No LGBT
-No whitewashed
-No Permadeath
-Controls are easy to learn, easy to master
-Keys are not part of the limited inventory
-They have now 3rd person option unlike from the RE7 that they forced player on their immersive blah blah blah
-They remove the cancer S Rank achievements in main story
-Village of Shadows: The hardest difficulty is not hard if you are careful
-Hardest difficulty does have autosaves and unlimited manual saves
-Biblical accurate angel main antagonist

CONS
-Speedrun achievements (this should remain on challenges not in steam achievements)
-Collectibles achievements are tiresome
-No Auto-sort Inventory
-Map is not interactive
-No Minimap option
-Lycan's howling are so loud specially later in the game it became annoyance
-in-game Challenges menu only appears once finished the game
-No stealth kill or takedowns
-No statistics for how many kills, deaths, saves or whatnot

Just finished the DLC (the main story too of course) and its an amazing game, big step-up from biohazard. R.I.P Ethan though, was a great main character, and I honestly would've liked to see more of him, but hey, a fitting end to his story I guess. I'd like to see how Rose would be introduced into the story later, if that would even be taken into consideration. Though the "End of Zoe" DLC is still the best by far, I cant glaze it enough, Joe the G.O.A.T.

I really liked the Duke as a merchant, probably my favourite honestly. He helped us throughout the story, and the addition of the food was pretty nice. Although I did accidentally sell the quality meat before I knew what the food menu thing even was so I couldn't get the best guard upgrade, but it's whatever, not like I used it anyways 😂. Though there are a few nit picks. Having to sort the inventory yourself out is pretty annoying, especially how you have to move the items it. Having to go into the inventory to use meds instead of using ctrl as well. The DLC lacked boss fights, had like 3, 1 of which you could count as not one, but it is a DLC so that can slide. The mutamycete disruptor ability whatever was a neat addition, not much more to say.

The map was amazing, detailed and fun to traverse. Graphics definitely improved. The boss fights in the main game were amazing as well. Heisenburgs was my favourite out the whole franchise so far, driving around in a makeshift tank with an infinite ammo machine gun and cannon was so hype. I also agreed with Heisenburg, not Ethan. So what if your daughter is going to be used to defeat Miranda? She is far more evil than Heisenburg, so i'd just say let him. I also didn't really see him as evil at the start, he genuinely tried to get Ethan on his side. The Beneviento fight was pretty mid, no words, the house and slimy baby creeped me the hell out though, definitely the scariest area in the game. Moreau's design was cool although disgusting. At some point you'd feel bad for hi…

Simply a fun game. Not a great game, not a bad game. Just a game that is unapologetically fun. There's enough challenges and extras you can mess with to keep the game entertaining through multiple playthroughs. This game is not high art, but it certainly is high entertainment. My only massive issue (and the only achievement I don't have as of the time of writing this review) with the gameplay is that Village of Shadows/Super Hard difficulty is extremely poorly balanced and not fun in the slightest. I enjoyed every other part of the game but a VoS run is simply torture.
But now let's talk about the story: It's there. The ending is really good. And the rest is just there.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the third-person perspective mode as clunky and poorly implemented.

citations.review_text: as my personal favourite resident evil game, i feel that this one has the most compelling story. especially when you play this and re7 back-to-back. i love the eerie feel and the re-playability is endless. you find new things every playthrough and also notice things you didn't realise before. if i had to say something somewhat negative it would be that the 3rd person view is a little bit clunky but it was obviously made for first person so its not that bad. in the end its a 10/10 game in my opinion and i highly recommend for anyone who wants a good, long and compelling story game

When you try stand up to the king, you best not miss. Makes itself too comparable to fourmake as a self disservice, or to look at it another way I'm glad they were able to fix everything for fourmake. 
Controls had quite a lot of issues, felt too stiff and no good way to set the controls in a natural way, also a nice sensitivity was between one that was way too low and way too high. Third person was also so poorly implemented, and I really think it would have been better in third person if it would have controlled like the remakes.
The story was fine but the scripting I had a lot of issues with, especially in the early stages. The segmentation of the story also didn't let the villain expand much as characters, definitely not as much as I would have liked, especially bad with the four Dimitrescus.
I did not like the voice direction they went with for Heisenberg, he was not nice to listen to.
Too many points of no return, getting sick of this.

Really like Beneviento's section, far and away the best one. The puzzles were fun and they didn't expand on her in a way that would leave you wanting more. The sections in the village were also great. Dimitrescu's and Moreau's section are also good, second tier but still good, just a few issues and too much combat through them.
The weapons were nice to use, majorly helped a long when I decided to get a 4x damage mod later in the campaign, should have known to have it on the whole time. On mods I also recommend the ADS mod, surprisingly well done and in active development so may be better by the time you play.
Weird thing to add but best flashbang effect I've seen in a video game, very visually interesting and if you headshot a larger enemy they look like the cover of Carpenter's The Thing.
 
High 7 / 10

claims.claim: Reviewers report that certain quests will hard-lock the player if progressed too far without warning.

citations.review_text:
TLDR: Just short of perfect, Resident Evil Village is a blast to play through; impactful combat, a compelling (yet zany) narrative, and gorgeous visuals create a stellar videogame. A must-play for the survival horror genre.

Pros: 
- Took real feedback from Resident Evil 7 and made the formula better.  
- A game world that's intriguing and rewarding to explore.
- Incredible presentation values; from the acting, to the visuals, to the sound design.
- Improves upon the messy story of RE7 and brings some true creativity to the enemy designs and environments. 
- New Game+ is sincerely fun to play; unlike most other games.  You'll want to unlock bonus content (which can be used to make seemingly impossible challenges possible!) 

Cons:
- Some quests will hard-lock you if you progress too far (without warning).
- The game hates HDR and refreshes resolutions on your monitor when exiting the options menu (????) 
- Some characters are killed off far too quickly... would have liked to have seen more of some of the minor antagonists.
- The story flounders a bit...but eventually has a satisfactory conclusion. 
- Some of the 'weirdness' of the franchise is ramped up to 100 in this game.  Flying dolls, Magneto-the-Cowboy, and giant-lady fetishes...to name a few instances.  I wish RE would stay a little more grounded in reality.  

Overall: 
9/10
